note: Preregistered experiment, 40 percent time reduction and 18 percent quality gain on professional writing tasks.
title: Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence

reading.body:
In a preregistered experiment on professional writing tasks, generative AI cut completion time by 40 percent while improving output quality by 18 percent.

Preregistration matters methodologically, it means the hypotheses and analysis plan were fixed before the results came in, which rules out one of the most common ways studies overstate an effect after the fact. Getting both a large time reduction and a quality improvement, rather than a speed and quality tradeoff, is also a stronger result than either finding alone.

The paper's tasks were professional writing specifically, so the 40 percent and 18 percent figures should not be assumed to generalize to other kinds of work without their own testing.

explain_beginner: Researchers tested whether ChatGPT could help professional workers write faster and better. They gave writing tasks to over 450 college-educated workers, letting half use ChatGPT while the other half could not. Workers with ChatGPT completed their tasks 40 percent quicker and produced work that was 18 percent higher quality. The tool also helped reduce skill differences among workers. After the experiment ended, workers who had tried ChatGPT kept using it in their actual jobs, suggesting the technology has real staying power.
explain_business: This research demonstrates that generative AI tools like ChatGPT deliver measurable productivity gains in professional writing work, specifically cutting task time by 40 percent while improving output quality by 18 percent. The findings indicate that skilled workers across different backgrounds benefit from the technology, narrowing performance gaps in the workforce. Strong post-experiment adoption rates suggest genuine business value. Organizations should consider that implementing such tools could accelerate project completion, improve work quality, and help standardize performance across teams with varying experience levels.
explain_practitioner: A preregistered randomized controlled experiment with 453 college-educated professionals assigned to occupation-specific, incentivized writing tasks evaluated ChatGPT's impact. Treatment participants received access to the chatbot while controls did not. Key findings included a 40 percent reduction in task completion time and 18 percent quality improvement measured against professional standards. Secondary outcomes showed decreased performance variance between workers, elevated AI sentiment, and sustained adoption behavior with workers in the treatment group showing 2.0x adoption rates at two weeks post-experiment and 1.6x rates at two months.
